course_description:
This course provides an opportunity for students to pursue in some depth an area of special interest under the supervision of a member of the Law School academic staff. Further guidelines are available from the Law School.

The course is a two unit elective, which offers students an opportunity to 1) design and 2) execute an individual research project under the supervision of an academic in the Law School. Participation is subject to coordinator approval and generally suitable for students with a cumulative GPA in Law of 5.5 or more.

As the course involves self-directed learning, students who undertake this course will be expected to be proactive. First, they will need to identify a question of doctrinal law, legal theory or socio-legal studies that they would like to explore. Second, they will need to arrange a potential supervisor and, having done so, complete and submit the enrolment form.

Once semester starts, students should watch/read the resources on Blackboard and the Library website to inform their research process, and arrange at least two meetings with their supervisors (one for each assessment item). There will be two presentation sessions as well.

Additional timetable information
The learning in this course is largely self-directed. Students will be expected to work through materials on legal research and writing on Blackboard and seek input from their academic supervisors on their proposals and final essays, as well as their plans for the presentation component. It is up to students to contact supervisors and not the other way around.
course_aims:
Education Mission Statement

The mission of the School of Law is to educate you in and about the law. We seek to assist you to think critically about the law and to investigate its structures, principles, policies, and values. This is achieved by engaging with you as fellow investigators in a range of critical and intellectual conversations about the law and its place in society. Our role is thus to guide you in your own intellectual journey in the law and to equip you with the necessary skills that will enable you to continue that journey long after you have left the School.

Course Aims

This course aims to allow students to undertake self-directed research under the guidance of a supervisor, as part of an ongoing research project, within a research team context.

learning_outcomes.description: Formulate a significant and novel research question in or across the fields of doctrinal law, legal theory or socio-legal studies.
Design a research project to investigate that question using appropriate approaches to legal research and methodologies.
Utilise legal writing techniques that are appropriate to different academic aims and audiences.
Manage research projects to produce quality work within time-constraints.

assessment_details.title: Proposal
assessment_details.task_description: The Research Proposal is a max 2,000-word description of your research project, which includes a draft outline of your research paper. The research proposal should identify the aims (question), scope and methodology/approach of the project, and position that project in its social and scholarly context. Headings are included in the word count, as are quotations. Footnotes do not if they only contain references. Read full task description Hide full task description
assessment_details.assessment_security: Open assessment: In this assessment you can use resources such as your notes, course materials, and other tools, including AI, while completing the task. The focus is not on memorising information, but on understanding, applying judgement, and demonstrating your own thinking.
assessment_details.submission_guidelines:
The Research Proposal should be submitted electronically on the Blackboard site.
Deferral or extension
You may be able to apply for an extension .
The maximum extension allowed is 7 days. Extensions are given in multiples of 24 hours.
Extension to Assessment Due Date
The maximum extension for an assessment item due within the semester / teaching period in which the course is offered is 7 days. In exceptional circumstances, an extension may be approved for a further 7 days. Where a student is incapacitated for a period longer than 14 days, they are advised to apply for removal of course.
A student may apply for an extension to assessment due date if they are unable to meet an assessment deadline due to extenuating circumstances. Please refer to the Applying for an extension page on my.UQ for further details on acceptable reasons for an extension and for instructions on how to apply . Additional information on extensions can be found within the Assessment Procedure .
Spoken or written notification of difficulties with assessment deadlines to a course coordinator or the School does not constitute an authorised extension.
Late submission
A penalty of 10% of the maximum possible mark will be deducted per 24 hours from time submission is due for up to 7 days. After 7 days, you will receive a mark of 0.
Penalties for Late Submission
The following penalties apply to late submission of an assessment item, assuming that an extension has not been approved, and that late submission is academically possible (e.g., it does not delay feedback to a cohort, or interfere with course delivery).
First 7 periods of 24 hours (or part thereof) - 10% per 24 hours of the maximum possible mark for the assessment item. For example, a report worth a maximum of 40 marks, submitted 28 hours late will attract a penalty of 8 marks, calculated as 2 periods of 24 hours x 10% x 40 marks.
More than 7 periods of 24 hours - 100%.

assessment_details.title: Research Reflections
assessment_details.due_date: 19/10/2026 - 23/10/2026 The exact time and place of the session will be posted on Blackboard at the start of semester.
assessment_details.task_description: In this task, you will deliver a 10-minute reflection on your research projects, as they have evolved during the semester. As a reflection, it is a presentation that will not only introduce your project -- its question, background, approach, findings -- to an academic but non-expert audience. In addition, it will discuss 1) how and why your research aims, questions, and method/approach have changed over the semester; 2) what parts of the research and writing process came most easily and were most challenging; and 3) how your actual findings and argument varied from your expectations. After each presentation there will be up to 10 mins Q&A, which is also assessable. Read full task description Hide full task description

You must only use the approved materials and tools for this assessment task. Use of prohibited materials in this task may be investigated and treated as academic misconduct. See assessment instructions for more details.

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 1 To Week 1 (27 Jul - 02 Aug)
learning_activities.topic: Getting started (Finalising supervision arrangements and self-directed learning) In Week 1, students will begin working through the self-directed learning modules about legal research and writing (see Blackboard for details) and meet their supervisors for an initial discussion. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 2 To Week 6 (03 Aug - 06 Sep)
learning_activities.topic: Independent research (Reading, Planning and Writing) Between Weeks 2 and 6, students should be reading into their topics, planning and writing their proposal under the guidance of their supervisors. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 7 To Week 13 (07 Sep - 01 Nov)
learning_activities.topic: Independent Research and Meeting with Supervisor (Reading, Planning and Writing) From Weeks 7 to 13, students will be undertaking independent research on their papers with guidance from their supervisors. The second compulsory meeting between students and supervisors must take place in this time, though multiple meetings will most likely be necessary for students to complete their Papers. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04
